name: HotelWorld AI: vendor page promoting the Q1 2026 World's Best at AI Index
title: HotelWorld AI: vendor page promoting the Q1 2026 World's Best at AI Index
answer: HotelWorld AI is a vendor site selling AI agents to hotels, and it also promotes the Q1 2026 update to its World's Best at AI Index. The most useful thing it states is the scale of that tracking: 2,105 or more hotel brands and 131,000 properties measured for how often they appear in AI-generated answers on ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity and Claude. Its argument is that travellers now ask an assistant and receive a shortlist rather than scanning links, so visibility inside those answers is becoming a competitive measure.

sections.body: HotelWorld AI publishes this page, which is a commercial landing page for the company's AI agents rather than a research document. It advertises agents for hotel back-office and guest-facing work, including an AI Search Agent and a Demand Intelligence Agent, and it promotes the Q1 2026 update to a report it calls the World's Best at AI Index. The stated scope of that index is global, covering hotel brands and their properties. The page names no author and gives no publication date beyond the Q1 2026 label on the index update. The text was harvested on 26 September 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page argues that AI assistants are changing how guests find hotels, and that the distribution playbook hotels have used for two decades no longer fits. Travellers, it says, no longer scroll through ten blue links but ask an AI and receive a shortlist, so hotels must adapt to stay visible, building on search engine optimisation with further optimisation for AI answers. To support that, HotelWorld AI promotes the Q1 2026 update to its World's Best at AI Index, which it says shows how hotel brands are moving inside AI-generated recommendations across ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity and Claude. The index, as described here, tracks more than 2,105 hotel brands and 131,000 properties worldwide, measuring which brands AI engines surface, how often they appear, how rankings move, and what those movements mean for hotel leaders. The page also mentions Leo, described as the company's AI search worker for hotels, and says it was built to start from the individual property and work up to the brand. Beyond these claims, the page presents no findings, rankings or named brands.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The page states that the Q1 2026 World's Best at AI Index tracks more than 2,105 hotel brands and 131,000 properties globally. It names ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity and Claude as the engines covered, and elsewhere lists Google AI Overview among the surfaces its agents address. It claims AI visibility is becoming the industry's next competitive battleground and that travellers now receive a shortlist instead of a list of links. The page gives no figure for the share of hotels that appear in AI-generated shortlists, and no rankings, scores or named brands.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in hospitality would use this page mainly as a pointer. It names a recurring index and a set of AI assistants that matter for hotel discovery, which helps frame answer-engine visibility as something that can be tracked over time rather than guessed at. It also shows a vendor positioning itself around that shift, with agents for search visibility and demand intelligence. Because the page reports the existence and scope of the index but not its results, it is useful for orientation and for finding the report, not for evidence about which brands actually lead.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Hospitality

sections.body: The page is commercial, published by a company selling the agents it describes, so its framing of AI discovery as an urgent problem serves its own product. It is a landing page with little substance: no methodology, no sample details, no results, no named brands and no link to the underlying data are given in the text. The only date is the Q1 2026 label on the index update, and the page carries no author. It does not cover other AI assistants beyond those named, nor any hospitality segment detail, nor any counterargument to its own claims.
